item.title: Four Seasons Kuda Huraa Opens a Private Island Dedicated to Naturopathic Wellness
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Four Seasons Resort Maldives at Kuda Huraa, wellness is moving beyond the traditional spa experience with the debut of ŪRJĀ Naturopathy Island, a dedicated wellness destination centered on naturopathic care, personalized guidance and sustainable wellbeing. Named for the Sanskrit word for vitality, ŪRJĀ combines naturopathic principles with scientific expertise, with programs designed around four core pathways: Rest & Rebalance, Cleanse, Nourish and Reconnect.

Reached by a traditional Maldivian dhoni from the resort’s main jetty, the island places wellness within a distinctly natural setting, with over-water treatment suites, open-air rituals and the surrounding ocean shaping the experience. Each journey begins with a naturopathic consultation, followed by individualized therapies, nutrition guidance and educational tools designed to help guests better understand their own wellbeing. Signature experiences include mud therapy, heliotherapy, sound healing, acupuncture and the Vagus Reset, while specialized programs address areas such as sleep, liver health and joint care. Yoga therapy is also offered as part of the program.

The Curated Take

ŪRJĀ is interesting because it treats a wellness retreat as an opportunity to learn, not simply unwind. The emphasis on consultation, education and practical habits gives the experience a more immersive dimension, while the private-island setting adds the kind of quiet and separation that can make meaningful restoration possible. For travelers increasingly looking for wellness experiences with a sense of purpose, the concept reflects a broader shift from the conventional spa escape toward more individualized approaches to wellbeing.

item.title: The Inn of The Five Graces Opens a Private Villa Inside One of Santa Fe’s Historic Homes
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Behind a weathered red gate in Santa Fe’s Barrio de Analco, The Inn of The Five Graces has unveiled Red Door, a private two-bedroom villa set within the historic Roque Tudesqui House. The approximately 2,000-square-foot residence offers guests the rare experience of staying inside a centuries-old adobe structure, with two private courtyards, a back deck, an expansive living room, dining room, kitchenette and richly appointed bedrooms. The house predates the Spanish colonial adobe era, with portions built using puddled adobe, an Indigenous construction technique that predates the introduction of Spanish-style adobe bricks.

Inside, Red Door reflects the distinctive design language of The Inn of The Five Graces, pairing historic architecture with rare antiques, custom textiles and intricate hand-laid mosaics collected from around the world. The villa’s secluded setting gives it the atmosphere of a private Santa Fe residence while retaining access to the inn’s hospitality and amenities. Adding another layer to the experience, the property’s celebrated wisteria, which cascades into purple blooms each June, is protected by a permanent preservation easement.

The Curated Take

Red Door is compelling precisely because the luxury here is inseparable from a sense of place. Rather than recreating Santa Fe’s history as décor, the villa places guests inside a building that has witnessed centuries of the city’s evolution. For travelers drawn to architecture, design and culturally layered stays, it offers something increasingly rare: the chance to experience Santa Fe not simply as a destination, but from within one of its historic homes.

item.title: Sa-Nga and Supattra Thai Dining Bring Regional Thai Flavors to One Intimate Dinner
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Centara Reserve Samui, Sa-Nga welcomed one of Koh Samui’s most celebrated Thai dining destinations, Supattra Thai Dining, for a one-night culinary collaboration on August 30. Known for its authentic Thai cuisine, locally sourced ingredients and deep appreciation for regional culinary traditions, Supattra joined Sa-Nga for an intimate seven-course dinner limited to just 18 guests.

The menu moved across Thailand’s diverse regional flavors, beginning with Sa-Nga’s Khao Yum Sa-Nga, followed by four dishes from Chef Supattra: Yum Pla, Nuea Mok, Gaeng Huaplee and Gaeng Puu. Sa-Nga closed the evening with Som Chun and Saku Lamyai. The collaboration brought together two culinary teams united by a shared approach to Thai gastronomy, balancing heritage, seasonality and craftsmanship with contemporary presentation.

The Curated Take

The appeal here is less about a special-event dinner and more about the opportunity to experience Thai cuisine through two distinct culinary perspectives. For travelers staying on Koh Samui, intimate collaborations like this offer a deeper introduction to the destination’s food culture, particularly when local chefs are given space to showcase the regional traditions and ingredients that shape their cooking.

item.title: Under the Full Moon, REVĪVŌ Bali Turns Wellness Into Ritual
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Each month, as the full moon rises over Bali, REVĪVŌ Wellness Resort Bali invites guests and the wider community to step away from the pace of everyday life with its Monthly Full Moon, Cacao & Sound Healing Ceremony. The recurring evening combines cacao, sound healing and mindful reflection in an intentionally unhurried ritual centered on the traditional symbolism of the full moon as a time of completion, release and renewal. Rather than filling the evening with activities, the experience creates space for participants to slow down, turn inward and reconnect with the present.

Held within the tranquil surroundings of the Nusa Dua wellness resort, the ceremony begins with cacao, described as a heart-opening ritual, before moving into immersive sound healing. Participants are encouraged to engage with the experience in their own way, whether seeking stillness, emotional release or simply a moment of deeper connection. The monthly gathering forms part of REVĪVŌ’s broader wellness calendar and offers a recurring opportunity to mark the transition between what has been and what comes next.

The Curated Take

There is something appealing about a wellness experience built around doing less. In a destination where itineraries can easily become packed with treatments, excursions and activities, REVĪVŌ’s full moon ceremony offers a deliberate pause. The ritual gives travelers a chance to experience Bali not through another scheduled activity, but through stillness, reflection and a connection to the rhythms of the natural world.

item.title: Meet Amelia, Boston Logan’s Holographic AI Concierge
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Navigating a busy airport may soon feel a little more like having a personal guide. Boston Logan International Airport has introduced Amelia, a life-size, hyper-realistic AI hologram designed to help passengers find gates, restaurants, shops, lounges and baggage claim through natural conversation. The pilot, launched by the Massachusetts Port Authority in partnership with Proto Hologram and Holomedia AI, combines a human-scale holographic presence with live mapping, airport information and real-time TSA wait times.

Amelia can communicate in up to 40 languages, with English, Spanish and French included in the initial service, and can connect travelers with a live customer service agent when human assistance is needed. Accessibility features include closed captioning, high-contrast displays, WCAG-compliant mapping and wheelchair-accessible positioning. The system is designed to remain available around the clock while helping airport staff focus on more complex passenger needs.

The Curated Take

The intriguing part of Amelia isn’t simply that she is a hologram. It is the attempt to make airport technology feel more intuitive and human at precisely the moment travelers tend to feel most disoriented. If passengers can ask a question naturally, see the route mapped in real time and still reach a human when necessary, the technology could make one of travel’s least glamorous rituals, getting through an airport, noticeably calmer.

item.title: A New Global Powerhouse for Curated Day Tours Takes Shape
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Three established names in guided travel, WalksDevour, Amigo Tours and Askos Tours, are joining forces under newly formed Flagship Group, creating a global platform designed to bring together leading day-tour operators while preserving the local expertise and identities that made them successful. The founder-led companies will continue operating under their existing brands and teams, but will share expertise and resources across guest experience, guide quality, product development, technology, marketing and operations. Flagship says additional partners are expected to join in the coming months.

The move brings together distinctly different approaches to experiencing a destination. WalksDevour is known for cultural, historical and culinary experiences in iconic destinations; Mexico-based Amigo Tours operates guided excursions across North America, Europe and Japan; and Italy’s Askos Tours specializes in small-group archaeological and cultural experiences around Naples, Pompeii, Sorrento and the Amalfi Coast. Backed by Shamrock Capital and with travel industry veterans Rod Cuthbert and Richard Prosser joining its board, Flagship is positioning the new group around a simple premise: scale can strengthen local expertise rather than replace it.

The Curated Take

There is an important distinction between creating a global tour company and creating a global collection of local specialists. Flagship’s house-of-brands approach could give travelers access to a broader range of deeply rooted experiences without erasing the personalities and expertise that make a great guide or local operator memorable. As travelers increasingly seek experiences that open doors into a destination rather than simply pass through its highlights, the people leading the tour may matter as much as the itinerary itself.

item.title: Tennessee’s Fall Foliage Offers New Reasons to Look Beyond the Smokies
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The Great Smoky Mountains may be Tennessee’s best-known autumn destination, but the state’s fall landscape extends well beyond its most visited national park. From East Tennessee’s mountain overlooks and scenic railways to Middle Tennessee’s waterfalls, historic parkways and harvest-colored plateaus, Tennessee is highlighting a collection of lesser-known places to experience the season. In the west, travelers can explore lakeside forests, botanical gardens and wildlife-rich wetlands, with opportunities ranging from kayaking and birdwatching to horseback riding and leisurely sunset drives.

Among the standout experiences are Roan Mountain State Park, where fall color typically peaks in mid-October and the night sky offers a different kind of spectacle; Fall Creek Falls State Park, home to dramatic waterfalls, extensive trails and overnight accommodations; and Reelfoot Lake State Park, where autumn scenery coincides with the arrival of migratory birds, including bald eagles. The Natchez Trace Parkway offers a particularly evocative road-trip route through Tennessee, while destinations such as Meeman-Shelby Forest State Park and Memphis Botanic Garden provide accessible ways to enjoy seasonal color near Memphis. Tennessee is also expanding access to the experience through colorblind viewfinders equipped with EnChroma lens technology at scenic locations across the state.

The Curated Take

Tennessee’s fall appeal lies in its variety. The state’s foliage can be experienced through a mountain hike, a quiet lake excursion, a historic road trip or a cultivated garden, allowing travelers to shape an autumn itinerary around their own pace and interests. The addition of colorblind viewfinders is especially meaningful, underscoring that the beauty of the season should be more accessible and inclusive rather than reserved for those who experience color in conventional ways.

item.title: At Oliverra Bali, a Cocktail Book Traces the Life of a Tree
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
At Oliverra, the signature clifftop restaurant and bar at Umana Bali, LXR Hotels & Resorts, cocktails become a way to explore Balinese philosophy, nature and the passage of time. The new The Life of the Tree cocktail book draws on Tri Hita Karana, the Balinese principle of harmony among the divine, humanity and the natural world. Its nine-drink collection follows the symbolic life cycle of a tree, moving from seed and roots through trunk, branches, flowers and fruit to fallen leaves, transformation and new beginnings.

Set against the limestone cliffs of Ungasan, where Mediterranean-inspired dining meets Bali’s tropical landscape, the collection combines layered spirits, house-made syrups, botanical infusions, tropical fruits and local aromatics. Each cocktail is intended to express a different mood or stage of life, from the sensory awakening of Namirasa and the grounded connection of Genitri to the reflective complexity of Niscaya, the floral elegance of Padmasari and the contemplative finish of Walmiki. The result is a bar experience designed to unfold through taste, presentation and storytelling rather than simply a list of drinks.

The Curated Take

The most intriguing aspect of The Life of the Tree is its invitation to slow down and consider a cocktail as a moment of ritual. By linking each drink to an idea such as growth, renewal, wisdom or letting go, Oliverra gives guests a more thoughtful way to engage with Balinese culture without separating it from the pleasures of the bar. It is a reminder that a sense of place can be expressed not only through architecture and cuisine, but also through what is poured into a glass.

item.title: Bali Moto Adventures Maps a New Route to Komodo for 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Bali Moto Adventures is inviting tour operators and travel advisors to bring a more adventurous side of Indonesia to their clients through its 2027 BALI2KOMODO CHALLENGE, a fully supported, 12-day motorcycle expedition across four islands. The journey travels east from Bali through Lombok, Sumbawa and Flores, covering remote landscapes, island crossings and culturally rich destinations before reaching the Komodo region. Seven scheduled departures are planned between March and October 2027, with private departures also available for partner groups.

Designed as a trade-ready product, the expedition includes motorcycles, fuel, accommodations, meals, riding equipment, a guide, mechanic and the logistical support required to navigate Indonesia’s island geography. Travelers can choose among three itinerary levels, ranging from a more comfort-focused experience with five-star accommodations and private boat transfers to longer, more rugged routes emphasizing distance and overland exploration. The programme also offers partner support, including complimentary places for a first departure and options for private groups and potential country exclusivity.

The Curated Take

Indonesia is often experienced through a single island or resort, but the BALI2KOMODO CHALLENGE presents the archipelago as a connected, constantly changing journey. The appeal is not simply arriving in Komodo, but earning the destination through a sequence of roads, ferries, villages, coastlines and landscapes that reveal a more expansive sense of place. For travelers who see the journey itself as the destination, this is Indonesia at a different pace and from a different vantage point.

item.title: Park Hyatt Sydney Welcomes a New Chapter of People-First Leadership
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Park Hyatt Sydney, long recognized for its extraordinary position overlooking the harbour and its understated approach to luxury, has welcomed Bastian Germer as its new General Manager. With a career spanning leading properties including Four Seasons Resort Maldives, Raffles Hotel Singapore, The Ritz-Carlton Osaka, The Ritz-Carlton Toronto, The New York EDITION and The Ritz-Carlton New York NoMad, Germer brings an international perspective shaped by a belief that the most memorable hospitality begins with genuine human connection.

His leadership philosophy was formed early, during childhood travels through Europe, when he became fascinated not simply by the destinations or hotels he visited, but by the seamless teamwork taking place behind the scenes. Today, he views luxury as less about ceremony and more about intention: thoughtful, intuitive service that makes guests feel understood. At Park Hyatt Sydney, Germer plans to build on the hotel’s legacy while fostering a workplace where colleagues feel supported, empowered and proud of their role in creating exceptional stays. He also sees Sydney’s creativity, culture and connection to nature as qualities that naturally complement the hotel’s sense of place.

The Curated Take

The most compelling detail in Germer’s story is that his understanding of luxury began with observing hotel employees rather than admiring hotel grandeur. His appointment offers a reminder that even the world’s most celebrated properties are ultimately defined by the people who create their atmosphere, anticipate needs and turn a spectacular setting into a meaningful experience.
